assessment.nobel_worthiness: The observation of a scalar boson consistent with the Higgs at the LHC is a clear discovery in nature that completed the Standard Model, and it is the experimental counterpart of the 2013 theory prize. Importance, clarity and lasting impact are beyond doubt. The question is whether the instrumentation and leadership of ATLAS and CMS, rather than the physics result alone, is the right object of recognition.
assessment.attribution: The credited names are the conceivers and long-time spokespersons or project leaders of the two experiments, a defensible way to honour a collaboration of thousands. Credit within such collaborations is inherently contested, and other leaders and the accelerator builders have claims. The three-person configuration is workable but not self-evident.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: more than a decade of independent confirmation by two experiments, with coupling measurements still tightening. Recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether the Committee should honour experiment leadership rather than the discovery itself
Fair allocation among many collaboration leaders and accelerator builders
Not independently verified here which individuals are best placed to represent each experiment

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and the opening of neutrino astronomy with IceCube is a genuine clue from nature: a new messenger, a diffuse flux, and association with the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane. A cubic-kilometre detector in Antarctic ice was a bold, original instrumental concept with lasting consequences.
assessment.attribution: Only one credited name, Francis Halzen, as the driving force behind IceCube. Many others (collaboration leaders, AMANDA pioneers, earlier proposers of deep-ice and deep-water detection) had important roles, so a single-laureate prize would need justification and possible additions outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature: the diffuse flux is firmly established by IceCube and corroborated by other analyses, and the source identification is growing but incomplete. Timing is good, though source origins remain open.
uncertainties: Sources of most of the neutrino flux are still unidentified
Single-name credit may understate the roles of other pioneers
Independence of confirmation from other detectors is still limited

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Time-reversal-invariant topological insulators are a conceptually original discovery (Z2 invariant, quantum spin Hall effect) with a rapid, striking experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells. They opened a new class of quantum matter and have a broad influence on condensed-matter physics and beyond.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele provided the decisive theory; Molenkamp led the experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall edge transport. Hasan has an important claim for three-dimensional topological insulators, so the credit is not unique, and Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang predicted the HgTe effect, which is outside the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Mature: many independent experiments across materials over about 15 to 20 years, with the framework stable. Practical applications remain modest, but the scientific impact is clear.
uncertainties: Competing claims for HgTe prediction and 3D topological insulators
Whether the supplied names fully cover the decisive contributors
Overlap with other topological-matter candidates may affect how the discovery is framed

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of X-ray and optical afterglows of gamma-ray bursts settled the long-standing question of their distance and showed they are cosmological, extremely energetic events. This is a classic discovery from nature with an existential dimension, linked to the deaths of massive stars and later to compact-object mergers.
assessment.attribution: BeppoSAX X-ray localisation by Costa and Frontera and the optical and radio follow-up led by Kulkarni's group are central. The late Jan van Paradijs and others (optical identification, redshift measurement) are also important, and the supplied names leave this partly unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Mature: nearly thirty years of confirmation by Swift and others, and a firm interpretation. Recognition is somewhat late, with the death of some key figures a complicating factor.
uncertainties: Contribution of deceased and other key contributors cannot be honoured
Allocation between satellite localisation and ground-based follow-up
Not independently verified who made the first optical identification

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP provided precision measurements of the CMB anisotropies that fixed the parameters of the standard cosmological model and gave strong evidence for dark energy and dark matter, the subject I find most compelling. The result is of lasting importance, though the Committee already honoured the CMB spectrum and anisotropy discovery (COBE, 2006).
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission, Spergel led the cosmological interpretation and Page was a key instrument scientist. The configuration is plausible, but the WMAP science team was large and Planck later superseded the data, which complicates the argument for a single-mission prize.
assessment.maturity: Mature and well confirmed by Planck and other CMB experiments, though the novelty beyond COBE and the supernova prize may be questioned.
uncertainties: Whether WMAP is sufficiently distinct from the 2006 CMB prize
Credit among the large science team and relation to Planck
Tensions in the standard model (Hubble tension) may affect how the legacy is framed

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Inflation is an enormously influential idea that explains flatness, horizon uniformity and the origin of structure through quantum fluctuations, and the observed spectrum of CMB anisotropies is consistent with it. Yet the mechanism itself has not been confirmed: primordial gravitational waves are not detected, and the model space is very flexible.
assessment.attribution: Guth proposed the scenario, Linde (new and chaotic inflation) and Mukhanov (quantum origin of fluctuations) are decisive, with Starobinsky, Albrecht and Steinhardt and others as competing claims excluded by the supplied credit. The allocation is disputed.
assessment.maturity: Partly mature: the predictions of nearly scale-invariant adiabatic Gaussian fluctuations are verified, but the decisive test (tensor modes) is missing. I am wary of honouring elegant theory before nature gives a clear clue, so this is possibly premature.
uncertainties: No detection of primordial B-modes
Credit disputes with Starobinsky, Albrecht, Steinhardt and others outside the supplied names
Alternative explanations are not excluded

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, with correlated insulators and superconductivity in flat moire bands, opened a major new platform and a large field of experiments. The combination of a precise theoretical prediction of flat bands and a striking experimental discovery is attractive.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the magic angle and flat bands, and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experimental discovery of correlated states and superconductivity. Cory Dean's group and others have strong claims, and Cao as first author is not credited.
assessment.maturity: Recognition would be somewhat early: the field is under 10 years old, the mechanism of superconductivity is still debated, and sample reproducibility and the interpretation are evolving.
uncertainties: Origin of superconductivity remains unsettled
Other experimental groups and early career researchers may have claims outside the supplied names
Timeliness: the field is still rapidly developing

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Baryon acoustic oscillations provide a standard ruler seen in galaxy clustering and now central to measuring cosmic expansion and dark energy, with recent hints of evolving dark energy that interest me. The detection in 2005 by SDSS and 2dFGRS was a clean observational result.
assessment.attribution: Eisenstein led the SDSS detection and Cole and Percival the 2dFGRS analysis, a reasonable pairing of two independent teams. The original theoretical prediction of the acoustic peak (Peebles, Yu, Sunyaev, Zeldovich) lies outside the supplied credit, and many team members contributed.
assessment.maturity: Mature as a method, with confirmation from several surveys, but the most exciting physical consequence for dark energy is still under active debate. The recognition may fit later, once the physics conclusion firms up.
uncertainties: Overlap with prior dark energy and CMB prizes
Whether the discovery is a measurement technique or a fundamental discovery
Current evidence on evolving dark energy is not settled
